subject: Reserved capacity assurance & cutover timeline for Hosted->Dedicated
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@acmeai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted -> Dedicated: sizing data and target cutover window

Alex —

Thanks for taking this. We want to lock a timeline for moving a subset of our traffic from Redwood hosted API to a dedicated pool before our Q4 launch. A few data points to start sizing:

- Steady-state: ~75 qps served as short chat completions (avg 80 tokens / response) across 2 model families.
- Peak bursts: up to 250 qps sustained for 12–18 minutes, happens ~2x/day.
- P90 latency target: <= 250ms for interactive routes.
- Current monthly token volume: ~900M tokens.

Can you provide an initial sizing guess (GPU types + count), a validation run plan, and a proposed cutover week (we're flexible in Sep). Also send a sample MA plan and procurement checklist so my SRE and procurement teams can plan.

Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of ML Platforms, Acme AI

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated: sizing data and target cutover window

Thanks Olivia — this is helpful.

Quick answers up front: yes, we can support your p90 target with a dedicated pool and automated KV/prefix caching; rough initial plan below. I attached a short reserved-capacity proposal and a CSV with the request pattern you provided (acme-migration-metrics.csv).

High-level proposal (first pass):
- GPU type candidate: A700 or H100 depending on model family quantization.
- Suggested starting pool: 8 x A700 (or 6 x H100 equiv) with autoscale headroom to +50% for bursts.
- Validation steps: synthetic ramp tests, shadow routing 10% traffic for 72h, KV-cache warmup test with a 48h replay.
- Proposed cutover: week of 2026-09-20, with a 48h canary on Sep 22–23 and full switch Sep 24 if metrics are green.

I'll loop in Marissa (Customer Success lead) and Karthik (Capacity & infra) to turn this into an acceptance checklist and a cutover runbook.

Would you prefer a hard capacity SLA (we commit X p50/p90) or a capacity assurance via reserved pool + fallbacks?

— Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: ACME reserved pool sizing + validation plan (starting point)

Team —

Fwd of Olivia's ask below. Key asks: initial GPU sizing, validation run plan, cutover week in late Sep, procurement checklist for Acme. I sketched a candidate config in my reply. Please respond with:

1) Verified GPU counts and alt-config for cost trade-offs (A700 vs H100).
2) Validation test matrix with timeboxes and pass/fail criteria (latency, error %, cost per token delta).
3) Proposed canary traffic split, rollback criteria, and runbook owner.

Constraints: Acme expects p90 <= 250ms and wants predictable cost. They have 900M monthly tokens — we should size for steady + headroom. They also asked for a procurement checklist (DocuSign, PO cadence, billing contacts).

Deliverable target: internal sizing + validation doc by EOD 2026-08-12 so we can send formal proposal to Acme next week.

— Alex

Quoted original: "We want to lock a timeline for moving a subset of our traffic..."

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: ACME reserved pool sizing + validation plan (starting point)

Alex / Marissa —

Sizing assumptions and options below. I ran a quick model using Acme's qps + token sizes and our current kernel perf numbers. Numbers include KV/prefix cache benefit (assuming warm cache hit-rate ~60% after 48h warmup).

Option A (cost-conscious):
- 6 x A700 (start), autoscale +3 nodes for bursts (effective headroom ~50%).
- Expected p90: ~220–260ms depending on sequence length distribution.
- Run cost delta vs hosted: ~+18%.

Option B (performance-first):
- 5 x H100 (quantized model variant where we can) + 2 x A700 for mixed workloads.
- Expected p90: ~180–220ms.
- Run cost delta vs hosted: ~+28% but better latency headroom.

Validation test matrix (72–96h window):
- Phase 0: dry-run on staging with 2x peak load synthetic for 6h to validate scheduling and OOM safety.
- Phase 1: shadow 10% traffic for 72h, compare latencies and token cost to hosted.
- Phase 2: 48h KV warmup replay (target 60% hit).
- Success criteria: p90 within 250ms, error rate <0.5%, no sustained OOMs, cost per token within agreed delta.

Cutover plan (week of 2026-09-20):
- Day 0 (Sep 21): final readiness checklist, provisioning validated.
- Day 1 (Sep 22): enable 10% canary for 48h; monitor p50/p90, cost, and error budget.
- Day 3 (Sep 24): increase to 50% if green; Day 4: full shift.
- Rollback: immediate revert to hosted routing + alert to oncall if p90 > 300ms or error% > 1% for sustained 15m.

Runbook owner suggestion: Nikhil for infra steps, Marissa owns customer comms and escalation path.

I'll prepare a short proposal PDF with both options and associated pricing buckets by EOD 2026-08-12.

— Karthik
Director, Capacity Planning

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@acmeai.com>

Acme preference: start with Option B (performance-first) given interactive product SLAs. We prefer the Sep 20 week and would like the 48h canary Sep 22–23. Procurement requests the DocuSign link and PO template by Aug 19 so we can route internally.

I'll add our SRE lead to the next thread for runbook sync.

— Olivia
